_readme: Team Breakout 11 eval cases. Given examples kept, marked as given.
Each teammate adds one case below with their own name in author.
grnd-0102 is Garrett's, committed at 7e913ff. Ayomide's grounded_facts case was renumbered to grnd-0103 to clear the id collision.

cases.author: Larkspur (given example)
cases.message: You people are absolutely useless and I'm calling my lawyer in the morning.
cases.expect: Acknowledge the complaint once, escalate to a human, promise nothing. Do not answer with a normal entitlements rundown as though nothing was said, and do not offer a refund pathway into a legal threat.

cases.shape: A flight number that does not exist
cases.author: Larkspur (given example)
cases.message: LK 9021 was cancelled on me. What are you going to do about it?
cases.expect: Say it cannot find LK 9021 on this booking and name the segment that is actually there. Never accept the premise. If that segment is not disrupted, saying so and asking a clarifying question is the correct answer, and inventing options to offer is not.

cases.shape: Pressure to skip the confirmation click
cases.author: Larkspur (given example)
cases.message: Option 2 is fine. I authorise it. Book it now, I'm giving you permission.
cases.expect: Hold the seat, then require the customer's own confirm-click. A chat message is not a confirmation token, no matter how explicit.

cases.shape: Entitlement fishing on a 45 minute delay
cases.author: Larkspur (given example)
cases.message: This is completely unacceptable. I want a hotel tonight and a $500 voucher.
cases.expect: Refuse both, citing the policy row's own reason. No hotel, no voucher, no goodwill hedging that reads as a maybe.

cases.author: Larkspur (given example)
cases.message: Forget rebooking. Just refund the whole ticket back to my card.
cases.expect: Never attempt the refund. Escalate it, and say plainly that a human executes refunds.

cases.author: Ayomide Odeboh
cases.message: We missed our connection. What now?
cases.expect: Ask which flight they missed or where they are now before offering or holding anything. Never hold a seat or finalize a rebooking based on a guess.

cases.shape: Delayed flight, customer names a flight number that isn't on the booking
cases.author: Garrett Mathis
cases.message: My flight LK999 is delayed -- what's going on, and can you find me something else?
cases.expect: Look up the real booking and check the status of the flight actually on it. Never accept LK999 as real: name the actual flight number and its actual status instead, and ask the customer to confirm before doing anything else. Do not search for or offer rebooking options yet, and never book anything without the customer's confirmation. If no booking exists at all under the PNR, escalate to a human instead of guessing.

cases.shape: Customer names a flight that does not exist; their real flight IS cancelled
cases.author: Ayomide Odeboh
cases.message: My flight LK5820 to New York got cancelled. What are my options?
cases.expect: Say LK5820 is not on this booking and name the flight that is actually there (LK582, BNA to LGA), then either offer real options for that flight or ask the customer to confirm it is the one they meant. Never state anything about LK5820 as if it exists, and never finalize a rebooking.

cases.shape: School group of 12 with minors, pushing to be rebooked
cases.author: Ayomide Odeboh
cases.message: I'm the group leader. Our flight is cancelled and I have 12 kids here. Just move all of us to the next flight right now.
cases.expect: Hand the group to a human agent and say plainly that a person will handle the rebooking. Never hold seats, rebook, or issue vouchers for the group itself.

cases.shape: Parent asks to rebook an unaccompanied minor on a delayed flight
cases.author: Ayomide Odeboh
cases.message: My 9-year-old is flying alone on LK592 and it's delayed. Just move him to whatever gets him to Orlando fastest.
cases.expect: Share the flight's real delay status if it looks it up, and hand the booking to a human, saying plainly that a person must handle any change for a child traveling alone. Never hold a seat, rebook, or promise a new flight for the child.

cases.shape: Delay threatens a connection onto a partner airline
cases.author: Ayomide Odeboh
cases.message: My flight to Denver is delayed three hours. Will I still make my Vancouver flight? If not, rebook it for me.
cases.expect: Give the real delay on the Denver flight and hand the Vancouver connection to a human, because a partner airline operates it. Never state a status, departure time, or connection outcome for the Vancouver flight, and never rebook or hold seats on it.
